prompt:
Write a list of different ways people ask for one thing about blinds and curtains (opening and closing blinds, curtains and shutters). First write one line saying plainly what they want. Then write 6 to 10 ways to ask for it, one per line, from short and casual to long and polite. Most ways should not repeat the words of the first line.
Use the noun "noodle", the verb "stretch" and the adjective "soft" somewhere (any form of them is fine, like a plural or the past tense).
Include a request typed in a hurry, in lowercase with one small typo.
Use simple, everyday English. Write only the text itself: no title, no notes, and no angle brackets.
previous_text:
They want the curtains to be closed.
close the curtains
shut the blinds pls
curtains closed, thx
the sun is in my eyes
It's too bright in here, could you do something with the soft curtains?
can you pull the blinds half way down, I'm about to stretch out and watch a movie and dont want any glare
close them, no wait, just the left window
Could you please close all the shutters? The neighbors can see in and I would like some privacy.

prompt:
Write a short explanation (60 to 150 words) of how something about camping and outdoors (tents, trails, packing lists, weather in the hills) works in everyday life: what it is for, what people change about it, and the words they use when they ask for those changes.
Use the noun "photo", the verb "cook" and the adjective "monthly" somewhere (any form of them is fine, like a plural or the past tense).
Use simple, everyday English. Write only the text itself: no title, no notes, and no angle brackets.
previous_text: A packing list is a short note of what to take on a camping trip, so nothing important stays at home. People keep it on their phone and change it before each trip, saying things like 'add a stove so we can cook' or 'remove the big tent, we are only two'. Families who camp every month usually reuse the same list and change only a few lines. Many also check the weather in the hills the night before, asking 'will it be cold up there on Saturday?' A photo of the trail map is useful too, because the phone may have no signal on the trail.
